In shaping the learning activities, the augmented reality authoring tools are paramount as they offer different affordances to non-technical educators that help them to author augmented reality learning scenarios. Unfortunately, the existing Augmented reality learning authoring tools are not accessible, removing the rightful benefits of users with disabilities. This research, therefore, used task scenarios, think-aloud protocol, system usability scale, and questionnaire to evaluate the accessibility of augmented reality learning authoring tool and identify the missing accessibility features for users with vision or hearing impairments. The evaluation results indicate that the development of an accessible authoring tool with the capacity to support users with disabilities is required.

articleTitle: SMS Connectivity and Information Display in 4IR Projects for Small-Scale Farmers
abstract: Smaller-scale communal or individual farming is underdeveloped in South Africa compared to commercial farming, which is well developed. Despite the increase of commercial agriculture, the agricultural expansion of smallholders is essential for long-term socioeconomic stability and food security. A smart farming culture is described in the fourth industrial revolution (4IR) for the agricultural site to boost productivity competitively. The 4IR concept combines artificial intelligence and big data, which have been very popular in precision farming and have been used to monitor, identify insect pests, detect soil moisture, determine when to harvest, and eliminate labour-intensive monitoring by people. A company that develops precision agriculture and its application is integrated into intelligent observation, which acquires real-time information from field-level data with minimum human participation. A sensor box will be constructed to receive and send SMSs using the GSM module, enabling small-scale farmers to connect with it and acquire time stamped data readings using basic cell phones that do not support cutting-edge technology and sophisticated software which can be used for forecasting. For the small-scale farmer to make educated agricultural decisions, the data containing the soil moisture conditions are supplied to a basic mobile phone through SMS upon request by sending a text to the wireless sensor node. As most small-scale farmers are people with limited to no knowledge and skills to use a computer and other related technology, and struggle with the idea of the internet of things, this eliminates the complicity of smart phone applications and advanced technology.

articleTitle: Immutable Livestock Tracking and Compliance Logs Using Blockchain
abstract: A supply chain is designed to maintain the quality of sensitive goods throughout their production process. The life cycle of a product requires different organizations, people, activities, information, and resources involved in the processing of a product or service from supply to customer.This paper describes a solution from e-Livestock (a software development company focused on livestock tracking) in collaboration with nChain (a blockchain technology development company), which enables small livestock producers to monitor and control the status of cuttle and collaborate with local regulatory entities. This solution uses the Bitcoin SV Blockchain to provide a tamper-proof and immutable sequential record of events such as vaccinations, asset ownership, and health tracking. Deployed in September 2022, it aims to prevent corruption, fraud, and human error by offering supply chain process improvements, achieving an end-to-end traceable model.

articleTitle: Implementing a Digital Health Information System During the COVID-19 Pandemic; a Stakeholder’s Approach from Kenya
abstract: Management of public health emergencies takes a multi-stakeholder approach and requires prompt and accurate data. To manage the COVID-19 data, the Kenyan Ministry of Health adopted the DHIS2 platform. Using a case study design, we used the stakeholder theory and data governance concepts to understand the implementation of the system. Data were collected through interviews at national and subnational levels. The main findings show that the DHIS2 had all the necessary support and capabilities to address all the COVID-19 data management activities but it was not effectively used due to coordination and governance issues. It was not easy to coordinate the multiple stakeholders with different interests and many of them continued using different systems including Microsoft Excel to achieve their data needs. The paper contributes to the emerging literature on digital platforms by identifying the pivotal importance of establishing adequate stakeholder engagement during emergencies

articleTitle: MaaS for Developing Countries: Local Engineers’ Assessment of its Feasibility
abstract: Mobility as a Service (MaaS) is a novel transport service delivery concept that aims to integrate multimodal transport services offered via digital platforms. The concept’s greatest promise is the creation of more sustainable transportation systems, where access and efficiency are prioritized. The concept may be used to accelerate development and overcome long-standing transport inequities but to date, very few studies have explored its applicability or viability to transport service delivery in the developing world. This study sought to fill this gap by examining the opportunities and challenges that exist for paratransit-based MaaS systems through engagements with transport engineers in Ghana. Using a questionnaire as an instrument, and mode and S.D as consensus criteria, the opinions of experts were collected and analyzed. From the results, it is clear that the viability of MaaS is unquestioned, however serious challenges to its implementation remain. Policy implications of these findings are discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Reversing Cyber Loneliness
abstract: After more than thirty years we reopen the folder of immersivity in a social dimension enabling creatives to express themselves in open public spaces. Is “immersivity” an interesting and innovative “communicative experience” to be enjoyed together with other citizens, breaking cyber-isolation. This paper describes a interdisciplinary Horizon Europe research project aimed to design and develop a cost effective, hassle-free, easy to install and tune solution to setup a multi-user, multisite, multi-platform non-invasive immersive and interactive users’ experiences, sorry for the long list of buzzwords identifying the key characteristics. The “users” are subdivided in two families: creative/authors and citizens. The first family is again subdivided by: authors without cyber skills and the couple creatives/programmers. The outcomes of the project includes specific training courses to enable both authors to express their creativity thanks to a simple procedure and already developed components or in case of cyber skilled users to integrate the open source platform with new ad-hoc created components.

articleTitle: Social Media Use of Personalised Persuasive Technology (PPT) Among African Students - Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Personalised Persuasive Technology (PPT) is popularly used to increase users’ engagement on social media. For users such as African university students, social media have become a common platform used for various activities such as entertainment, study, news, and communication. The aim of this study was to determine the impact of persuasive technologies used by social media platforms on African university students. Current literature is limited in demonstrating the effect of social media platforms’ use of personalised compelling technologies on African university students. Previous studies have focused on students at western universities. Therefore, this study focused on conducting a systematic literature review of the existing literature. The study identified the various PPTs used by social media, the methods used to employ the PPTs, and the impact they have on African students. This systematic literature review identified gaps in current research on the use of Personalised Persuasive Technologies used by social media platforms targeted towards African university students and the outcome of the study highlighted opportunities for further study about persuasive strategies relevant to African university students by social media platforms The systematic literature review revealed that there is a dire need for further studies on the effect of the use of PPT by social media on African university students.

Author Keywords: social media and African university students
